steps.title: Welcome
steps.body: A short setup to get this app ready. Nothing here is required; you can close it and come back later.

steps.title: Which kind of organisation is this for?
steps.body: Pick the organisation this app runs for. You get a worked example of it: bodies, meetings, decisions and templates that fit. Pick several if you want to compare them. Installing the app plants nothing on its own, so this step is the only one that adds data. Choose "None" on a production install.

steps.title: Load the example data
steps.body: Loads the sets you picked. The data is obviously sample data, it is safe to run more than once, and you can delete it afterwards.

steps.title: Welcome to Decidiq
steps.body: Let's take a quick spin through decision-making. We'll schedule a meeting together so you can see how the pieces fit, and you'll add the record yourself.
Meetings are the heart of Decidiq. Open Meetings from the menu to see everything on the agenda.
Schedule your first meeting. Give it a title and a date, then save. You can add agenda items, motions and decisions later.
steps.task: Click New and save a meeting

steps.title: Where the automation lives
steps.body: Flows are what happens without anyone clicking: a reminder before a deadline passes, a confirmation sent on submission. This is where you read and edit them. Nothing to build now.

steps.title: Your first meeting is scheduled
steps.body: Decisions, Tasks and Commitments, your Organisation and shared Registers are one click away in the menu. The documentation covers the rest.
steps.task: Open the documentation to keep going

store._note: Decidiq's store exchanges CONFIGURATION, not rows. A configuration set carries the registers, schemas, objects, views, flows, sources and mappings that make one way of governing work together, which is what someone means by a default gemeente. `types` selects that path (store-over-federated-config); an app declaring none keeps the remote objects API. `builtIn` names the four example sets already in lib/Settings/profiles/, so the page states what decidiq ships rather than rendering blank without a registry. There is deliberately no `installable` allowlist: a set exists to introduce schemas the instance does not have yet, so a list of schemas decidiq already owns would refuse exactly the sets worth installing. The trust boundary for a bundle is its publisher, enforced by the engine's source allowlist and trusted-key check.

observability._note: Decidiq adopts the OpenRegister AppHost observability engine (ADR-040 / ADR-006). The /api/health route is served by a thin GenericHealthController subclass (HealthController) that reshapes the engine result into the published REQ-API-004 body {status, baseUrl, version, openregister}; /api/metrics is aliased straight to GenericMetricsController. statusCodePolicy=always200 + cors=true reproduce the REQ-API-004 reverse-proxy probe contract (probes succeed even when degraded; CORS + OPTIONS preflight). The orAvailable check subsumes the former hand-rolled DI-container ObjectService lookup. No metrics[] descriptors: decidiq gains the implicit decidesk_info / decidesk_up gauges, a pure compliance upgrade over the no-metrics-endpoint baseline.

widgets._note: openspec/specs/dashboard/spec.md REQ 'KPI Cards' specifies all FOUR Row-1 cards as type 'custom' with a bespoke slot component (ActiveDecisionsKpiWidget / UpcomingMeetingsKpiWidget / PendingVotesKpiWidget / OverdueActionsKpiWidget). Only pending-votes-kpi was ever wired that way; the other three were left as declarative 'stat' widgets, so their .vue files were never mounted and the data-testids the spec asserts (active-decisions-kpi, upcoming-meetings-kpi, overdue-actions-kpi) existed nowhere in the DOM. Declarative 'stat' was also the wrong engine for these counts: as the open-toezeggingen-overdue note below records, OpenRegister's aggregation endpoint honours only scalar-equality filters, so the multi-value and relative-date filters these three declared could not be evaluated. The custom widgets self-fetch and compute client-side.
widgets.title: Decisions
Commitments over deadline
widgets._note: REQ-007 / design D6. Counts non-terminal toezeggingen (lifecycle open/in-uitvoering) whose deadline is past, and deep-links to the Toezeggingen index pre-filtered to the same non-terminal set. LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-18 (OR aggregation limitation): the stat-widget count endpoint (/api/objects/aggregations) honors ONLY scalar-equality filters (filter[lifecycle]=scheduled works). Multi-value filters do NOT work: a bare array (filter[lifecycle][]=…) is IGNORED (raw schema count 3), and the documented `in` operator (filter[lifecycle][in][]=…) returns 0. The @now relative token is unresolved. Root cause is in OpenRegister's AggregationRunner filter→SQL path (actively under change by a parallel session). The `in` form kept here is the documented-correct declarative intent (AggregationQuery supports scalar-eq + in/notIn/gt/gte/lt/lte/ne) and will yield 2 once OR handles multi-value; until then this KPI reads 0. Exact deadline<now overdue cut lives on the pre-filtered index via the search endpoint. Interim options if a non-zero KPI is required before the OR fix: single scalar filter {lifecycle:open} (partial), or a materialized boolean field filtered by equality. A layout entry is appended at the bottom band of config.layout; final top-row placement is a UI-validation call.

openspec/specs/dashboard/spec.md REQ 'Upcoming Meetings Widget' requires body name and agenda-item count per row and a highlight for meetings inside 24h. A declarative object-list renders columns from one schema and can do none of that, so UpcomingMeetingsListWidget.vue was built for it — and then never referenced, leaving the component orphaned and the spec'd behaviour absent.
widgets.title: Upcoming meetings

widgets._note: openspec/specs/dashboard/spec.md REQ 'Recent Decisions Widget' requires an outcome badge (adopted/rejected/'undecided' when outcome is null) and a publication-status badge per row, over the latest 10. A declarative object-list renders plain column values and cannot express either badge, which is why RecentDecisionsWidget.vue exists; it was never referenced from here.

widgets._note: Row 5 of the spec'd v2 grid. Both entries were specified in openspec/specs/dashboard/spec.md ('Row 5 (gridY=14, gridHeight=4): minutes-in-review (6 cols, stats-block, the only stats-block in the layout) and governance-health (6 cols, custom, slot: GovernanceHealthWidget)') and neither existed in this manifest at all, so the whole row was missing from the rendered dashboard. layout._note: Moved down from gridY=14 to make room for the spec'd Row 5 (minutes-in-review + governance-health, which together span all 12 columns at gridY=14). This KPI is an addition from the toezeggingen change and is not part of the five-row v2 layout in openspec/specs/dashboard/spec.md, so it gets its own band below it rather than displacing a spec'd widget.

config._note: Governance body (council, committee, board) — the standing organiser that owns meetings, members and a process template. Bespoke layout: body details lead (mandate, quorum rule, voting default, term dates, hourly rate) 8-wide with the Members roster surfaced right (member management is the daily task on a body), then the body's meetings as a full-width object-list so a clerk sees the meeting cadence at a glance, a Documents leaf for charters/standing orders, and the Process template / Efficiency analytics / Recording retention specialist surfaces below (moved out of the sidebar per the audit-only sidebar rule; each is a rarer, second-tier task so they sit lower on the page). Sidebar is audit-trail only. AUDIT FIX: `body-data` shows all 11 GovernanceBody fields at 2 columns — ceil(11/2)=6 rows left zero spare row for the card's own title/header, clipping the bottom field row; bumped to gridHeight 7 and the column below (`body-members` + the rest of the left-column stack) recomputed to stay flush. A shared-lib fix for this header-row accounting is coming for the general case; this is the blatant-undersizing exception called out for this page. ORGANISATION HUB (organisation-facet-composition): 8 read-only object-list facets appended below the existing 8 widgets — retirement schedule/term rules (appointments-and-terms, filter `body`), other positions/gifts (interests-and-integrity, filter `governanceBody`), participating organisations/shared-body participations (shared-governance-bodies, filter `sharedBody`/`participant` — no rowRoute, `widget:"link"` column resolves to the referenced body's own GovernanceBodyDetail per CnObjectListWidget's documented column pass-through), zienswijze rounds (shared-governance-bodies, filter `sharedBody`), and factions (governance-body itself, filter `parentBody`+`bodyType=faction`, rowRoute back into GovernanceBodyDetail). Every facet reuses an existing index/detail page; none introduces a new Vue component (design.md Decision 2). Laid out as 4 rows of 2 half-width (6-col) widgets starting at gridY 29.

config._note: actionsComponent injects the Table/Calendar segmented control (configurable-types-domain-model). CnIndexPage offers table/cards/list/map and its viewMode validator rejects anything else, so a calendar cannot be a shared view mode without editing @conduction/nextcloud-vue, which a leaf app must not fork; the toggle routes to the sibling MeetingsCalendar page instead and leaves this table untouched. The new `type` reference is DELIBERATELY NOT a column here: an index cell renders a reference as its raw uuid, and a table of uuids is worse than no column at all. It is surfaced on MeetingDetail, where the reference resolves. Restoring it as a column needs a `meetingTypeName` formatter of dossiq's lookupRelatedName shape, which decidiq has no formatter plumbing for yet — that is the follow-up, not a silent omission.

pages.title: Meetings
pages._note: type:"custom" because no typed archetype fits. This is not a list, a record or a widget grid — it is a month grid of 42 date cells that places meetings by scheduledDate, which no index/detail/dashboard page component renders. The typed alternative would be an index page in a `calendar` view mode, and that is genuinely where this belongs: CnIndexPage already carries table/cards/list/map. It is custom here only because its viewMode validator rejects `calendar` and @conduction/nextcloud-vue is owned by another change this wave — a leaf app must not fork the shared library to add a view mode. RETIRE THIS PAGE when the shared calendar view mode lands: the table page keeps its config, gains `calendar` in viewModes, and this page and its toggle both delete. The table surface (page id Meetings) is untouched and remains the typed index.

config._note: The calendar half of the meeting index (configurable-types-domain-model). A meeting is an event and a table is the wrong primary shape for one, but the table sorts and filters better — so this is a SECOND view, not a replacement, reached through the same MeetingViewToggle that sits on the index. Declared ABOVE MeetingDetail on purpose: /meetings/calendar must match before /meetings/:id, or the detail route would swallow it and render a 404 for the literal id "calendar".

Meeting — the operational hub of the app: the event that runs an agenda, gathers participants, produces minutes and decisions. Bespoke meeting-workspace layout: meeting fields split field-scoped (ADR-062 rule 3) into Planning (type, body, schedule, location, mode, chair, quorum, series, submission deadline — everything set BEFORE the meeting runs) 8-wide, and a thin Outcome strip below it (lifecycle, opened/closed timestamps, actual cost — everything only known AFTER/DURING the meeting) so neither widget clips or leaves dead cells; a Meeting stats KPI card and the live Participants roster stand right of both (who is expected/attending is the first thing a clerk checks); the ordered Agenda (agenda-item children keyed on `meeting`) sits full-width as the working document; Decisions taken and Minutes drafted render below as the meeting's outputs; a Documents leaf holds packets/attachments; the Votes aggregate and Publication actions render below the files (post-meeting outputs), with the lower-frequency Recurring series and Transcription surfaces at the bottom. No comms leaf on the body (the meeting schema declares no email/calendar/talk linkedType; calendar/Talk stay in the Integrations surface). Sidebar is audit-trail only. AUDIT FIX (visual-audit follow-ups): every `type:"custom"` widget on this page (participants/agenda/decisions/minutes/votes/publication/series/transcription) resolved to the CnDetailPage 'unavailable placeholder' because the page had no top-level `slots` map wiring `widget-<id>` to its registry component name (the ADR-062-rule pattern the manifest-v2 schema validator only enforces on `type:"dashboard"` pages) — that silent gap, not a data problem, produced the empty right column and the dead band above Documents; the `slots` block below fixes it. The new `meeting-stats` KPI card counts agenda items and action items via their real `meeting` FK property (verified in lib/Settings/decidesk_register.json); Decision carries NO `meeting` FK in the schema (only AgendaItem and ActionItem do) so a meeting-scoped Decisions count is not addable declaratively and is intentionally omitted. Participant likewise carries no `meeting` FK (only `governanceBody`) so no participants object-list collection is added — the existing MeetingParticipantsTab custom widget (now rendering, since it's wired via `slots`) covers the roster via its own `meetings`-array-based fetch. meeting-facet-composition adds 5 more meeting-scoped facets below the existing 12, closing the gap where wave-1 (ia-six-clusters) relocated oral-questions/interpellations/proxy-authorizations/kascommissie/routed-documents into the Meetings nav cluster without composing them onto this workspace: proxy authorizations (proxy-authorization.meeting) is a plain object-list widget with add-in-context; the oral-questions and interpellations facets that sat beside it were REMOVED by questions-as-agenda-items, which collapsed both schemas into agenda-item — those items now appear in the Agenda widget above, where the Type column names the configurable kind, so a per-kind facet here would list the same rows twice and would have to hardcode a seeded type uuid to do it; kascommissie verklaringen needs a thin wrapper (MeetingAuditStatementTab) because no manifest primitive gates a widget's visibility on organisatie_modus; routed incoming documents needs a thin wrapper (MeetingRoutedDocumentsTab) because it is a two-hop join (Meeting's own AgendaItems, then raadsinformatiebrief/ingekomen-stuk referencing those AgendaItems) no single declarative `filter` can express. THIS PAGE IS EDITED DIRECTLY, NOT via a manifest.d fragment (design.md Decision 1) — a fragment declaring `MeetingDetail` would REPLACE the page's widgets/layout wholesale (`mergePages` is by-id, not a deep merge), silently dropping every widget documented in this note.

pages.title: Meeting integrations

config.description: External integrations linked to this meeting. The Action items board (Deck), Discussion (Talk), files and notes appear on the page itself; linked articles, tags and the audit trail stay in the sidebar.

pages._note: Comms/collaboration workspace for a meeting — the ADR-019 integration surface, deliberately distinct from the MeetingDetail record page. The leaves promoted onto the body are exactly the providers bound to the meeting object through the registry: the Deck action-items board (migrate-action-items-to-deck-leaf), projecting the CalDAV VTODO ActionItems (ADR-002 source of truth) as cards and replacing the retired in-app TaskService/DelegationService board; Discussion (Talk); meeting Files and Notes. Comms leaves are legitimate here because these are the meeting's registry-bound integration providers. The useRegistry sidebar still lists every provider and hides each gracefully when its backing app is absent — action items then remain reachable via the Nextcloud Tasks app over the same VTODOs.

pages.title: Decision integrations

config.description: External integrations linked to this decision dossier. Linked emails, the Action items board (Deck) and files appear on the page itself; notes, tags and the audit trail stay in the sidebar.

pages._note: Email linking is consumed from the ADR-019 Email integration leaf bound to the decision object (migrate-email-links-to-email-leaf), replacing the retired in-app EmailLink store. The Action items board is consumed from the ADR-019 Deck integration leaf bound to the decision object (migrate-action-items-to-deck-leaf), projecting CalDAV VTODO ActionItems (ADR-002) as cards and replacing the retired in-app TaskService/DelegationService board. The registry hides each tab gracefully when its backing app is absent — action items then remain reachable via the Nextcloud Tasks app over the same VTODOs.

pages.title: Agenda item integrations

config.description: External integrations linked to this agenda item. Linked emails, files and tasks appear on the page itself; notes, tags and the audit trail stay in the sidebar.

pages._note: Email linking is consumed from the ADR-019 Email integration leaf bound to the agenda-item object (migrate-email-links-to-email-leaf), replacing the retired in-app EmailLink store. Registry hides the Email tab gracefully when Mail is absent.

pages.title: Live meeting
pages._note: Realtime meeting shell — WebSocket subscriptions, frame-by-frame UI, per-vote-card animations. No typed primitive analogue; documented as the canonical example for a future type:realtime lib extension. See src/views/LiveMeeting.vue.

config._note: Participant — a person archetype (name, role, party, email, voting weight, attendance, linked Nextcloud user, join/leave dates). Bespoke person layout: contact/role details lead 8-wide with Related right (the meetings, votes and decisions this person is linked to across the register); a Documents leaf holds credentials/mandate letters. Deliberately NO Email or Calendar body leaf: the participant schema declares no email/calendar linkedType (the email address is a plain data field, and correspondence lives on the meeting/decision integration surfaces, not per-participant), so per the comms-leaf hard rule they are omitted. Audit trail stays a sidebar tab. AUDIT FIX: `participant-data` shows all 11 Participant fields at 2 columns — ceil(11/2)=6 rows left zero spare row for the card's own title/header, clipping the bottom field row; bumped to gridHeight 7 and the column below/right recomputed to stay flush.

Agenda item — one ordered line of a meeting's agenda (type, order number, estimated/actual duration, description, recurrence, parent item). Bespoke layout: item details lead 8-wide with a Documents leaf right for the supporting stukken (memo, annex) that back the item; the Motions tabled under this item (AgendaMotionsTab — decisions of decisionType=motion keyed on `agendaItem`) render full-width below because debating/voting motions is the whole point of an agenda item. Audit trail stays a sidebar tab; email/files linking lives on the dedicated AgendaItemIntegrations surface. AUDIT FIX: `agenda-data` shows all 10 AgendaItem fields at 2 columns — ceil(10/2)=5 rows left zero spare row for the card's own title/header, clipping the bottom field row; bumped to gridHeight 6 (and `agenda-files` matched to stay level in the same row) with `agenda-motions` recomputed to stay flush below.

pages.title: Motions
pages._note: decision-types-as-configuration: the built-in create/edit dialog reads properties.decisionType.enum from the stored schema, which is deliberately empty since #1099 (the decision_types app config is the only authority), so its type picker rendered 'No results'. DecisionFormDialog is the same CnFormDialog over the same schema, with the vocabulary fetched from GET /api/v1/decision-types through the shared decisionLink.js helpers (#1104) and spliced in client-side. The note stays a SIBLING of slots: CnPageRenderer resolves every slots entry as a registry name and warns on one it cannot find.

decision-types-as-configuration: same wiring and same reason as DecisionDetail. This page renders the Decision schema too, so its built-in Edit dialog showed an empty decisionType picker until the form-dialog slot (nextcloud-vue#944) let DecisionFormDialog splice the registry vocabulary in.
pages.title: Motion

config._note: Motion — a deliberative proposal (a Decision of decisionType=motion): proposer, motion type, proposed text, lifecycle, co-signers, submission date. The decision schema is a 42-field polymorphic supertype shared with Decision/Amendment; the data widget scopes to `content.include` of the 9 motion-relevant fields (ADR-062 rule 3) so decision-only fields (legalBasis, publishedAt, resolutionNumber, contract offer/order/product, etc.) that never apply to decisionType=motion don't clip the cell. Bespoke deliberation layout: motion details/text lead 8-wide with a Documents leaf right for the tabled text and annexes; the Amendments proposed against it (MotionAmendmentsTab — decisions keyed on `parentMotion`) render full-width because processing amendments is the core motion workflow; the Votes result (MotionVotesTab, read-only post-ballot aggregate) sits below, followed by the chair's amendment Voting order and the Voting round mechanics (procedural, so placed lowest). Discussion/Talk lives on the dedicated MotionIntegrations surface. Sidebar is audit-trail only.

pages.title: Motion integrations

config.description: External integrations linked to this motion. Open the sidebar for Discussion (Talk), files, notes, tags, tasks and the audit trail.

pages._note: Discussion is consumed from the ADR-019 Talk integration leaf bound to the motion object (migrate-comments-to-talk-leaf), replacing the retired in-app CommentService. Registry hides the Talk tab gracefully when Talk is absent.

pages.title: Amendment

config._note: Amendment — a proposed text change to a parent motion (a Decision of decisionType=amendment): proposed text, proposer, parent motion reference, voting order. `amend-data` scopes `content.include` to the 7 amendment-relevant decision fields (ADR-062 rule 3), same polymorphic-schema rationale as Motion. Bespoke amendment layout: the visual Text-changes diff against the parent motion (AmendmentDiffTab) is the reason this record exists, so it leads full-width; the amendment's own metadata (proposer, lifecycle, order) sits 8-wide below with the Parent motion link (AmendmentParentMotionTab) right so a clerk can jump back to the motion being amended. Audit trail stays a sidebar tab. No comms leaf — the amendment schema declares none; discussion happens on the parent motion. AUDIT FIX: the ~280px hole previously visible ABOVE the first (visibly-rendering) card was the full-width `amend-diff` cell (gridY 0-6) rendering CnDetailPage's 'unavailable placeholder' — this page had no top-level `slots` map wiring `widget-amend-diff`/`widget-amend-parent` to their registry component names, so both `type:"custom"` widgets rendered blank while still reserving their declared grid rows. The `slots` block below fixes it; content now starts at gridY 0 as declared.

pages._note: decision-types-as-configuration: same wiring and same reason as DecisionDetail. This page renders the Decision schema too, so its built-in Edit dialog showed an empty decisionType picker until the form-dialog slot (nextcloud-vue#944) let DecisionFormDialog splice the registry vocabulary in.

config._note: Minutes — the formal document record of a meeting (title, lifecycle, content, version, signers, approval date, generated documents). Bespoke document archetype: minutes metadata leads 8-wide with the Approval workflow (MinutesApprovalTab — lifecycle timeline with guarded submit/approve/reject and correction suggestions) right, because getting minutes approved is the primary task on this record; the generated Documents (MinutesDocumentTab — PDF/notarial packages written into the meeting Files folder) render full-width below as the tangible output, followed by the Signers roster and Publication actions (lower-frequency, so placed lowest). No comms leaf — the minutes schema declares none. Sidebar is audit-trail only.

pages.title: Decisions
pages._note: Same wiring as the Motions page, and for the same reason: the stored decision schema carries no decisionType enum since #1099, so the built-in dialog's type picker rendered 'No results'. DecisionFormDialog feeds the picker from the decision_types registry via the shared decisionLink.js helpers (#1104).

config._motionsFilterNote: REQ-RMN-003 — Motions is one decisionType of the unified Decision supertype (ADR-005), not a sibling concept. This quick-filter surfaces Motions AS a filtered view of Decisions (decisionType=motion, a STORED/queryable field merged server-side into the OpenRegister fetch — no client-side derivation, unlike effectiveStatus per the _inForceFilterNote). The retained Motions index page (pages[] id `Motions`, route /motions) carries the same filter plus motion-specific columns/tabs; the `page`/`route` hints let the strip deep-link there. The standalone top-level Motions menu leaf was retired (REQ-RMN-001) so Motions is reachable through its parent Decisions surface rather than as a peer top-level item.
config._inForceFilterNote: DESIGN D3 — the in-force filter operates over the derived effectiveStatus, which (per design D2) is NOT a stored/queryable field: OpenRegister cannot express the inbound supersedes/repeals lookup as a materialised calculation, so effectiveStatus is computed client-side. A static manifest `filter` (the proven Motions decisionType pattern) and `quickFilters` both merge a filter map into the OpenRegister fetch and therefore only work over STORED fields — neither can server-filter on a client-derived value. The in-force / superseded / repealed state is instead surfaced per-decision via the effectiveStatus badge column (computed client-side) plus the banner and incoming-relation groups in RelatedDecisionsTab. A server-side in-force filter becomes available only if/when effectiveStatus is materialised by an OpenRegister inverse-relation calculation operator (D2 follow-up).

pages._note: decision-types-as-configuration: this detail page's built-in Edit dialog renders the same Decision schema the index pages do, and #1099 deliberately emptied properties.decisionType.enum (the decision_types app config is the only authority), so its type picker offered nothing and the required field blocked the save. #1109 fixed the two index pages through CnIndexPage's form-dialog slot; CnDetailPage grew the same slot with the same scope in nextcloud-vue#944, so the same DecisionFormDialog is wired here rather than a second copy of the vocabulary logic. The note stays a SIBLING of slots: CnPageRenderer resolves every slots entry as a registry name and warns on one it cannot find.
pages.title: Decision

config._note: Decision — the core governance dossier (title, text, outcome, decision date, legal basis, lifecycle, publication state, effectiveStatus). The 42-field decision schema is split field-scoped (ADR-062 rule 3) into Content (title/text/proposedText/fullText/background/proposer/co-signers/resolution — WHAT was decided) and Governance (decisionDate/outcome/publication/lifecycle/enactedAt/voting mechanics/adoption+effective dates — the process STATE the dossier is in); fields already shown by dedicated tabs (amends/supersedes/repeals/route/offer/order/product, sourceApp/subject*/externalReference system fields) stay excluded from both. Bespoke dossier layout: Content leads 8-wide with the Lifecycle state machine (DecisionLifecycleTab — the guarded transition buttons that advance the decision) right, because moving a decision through its states is the primary action; Governance sits below Content with a Documents leaf beside it; the Action items it spawns (ActionItemsSurface — the Deck-board projection of children keyed on `decision`, ADR-019/ADR-002) render full-width, then Related decisions (RelatedDecisionsTab — the supersedes/repeals graph driving the computed effectiveStatus banner) and Route share a row, followed by the lower-frequency Voting results and Publication surfaces. Email linking lives on the dedicated DecisionIntegrations surface (schema declares no comms linkedType). Sidebar is audit-trail only. decision-facet-composition adds 8 reverse-lookup `object-list` widgets below the existing 9, grouped in 3 rows by domain (consultations: public/member/WOR; opinions+participation: advisory opinions/zienswijzerondes/zienswijzen; outcomes: commitments/confidentiality) so opening a decision surfaces everything that already references it via `decision`/`relatedDecision`/`relatedMotion`/`targetDecision` on six sibling schemas, closing the reverse-lookup gap `constituency-consultation`'s own manifest fragment deferred. Confidentiality is read-only (`allowCreate:false` — a restriction is imposed through the confidentiality register's own flow, not from here).

config._note: Action item — a task/case archetype spawned by a decision or meeting (title, description, assignee, due date, status, completion). Note the canonical store is a CalDAV VTODO (ADR-002) surfaced through the Deck leaf; this OR-backed detail shows the projected record. Bespoke task layout: task details (status, assignee, due date) lead 8-wide with a Documents leaf right for evidence/deliverables of completion, and Related below linking back to the originating decision/meeting. No comms leaf — the action-item schema declares none; assignment happens via the assignee field. Audit trail stays a sidebar tab.

pages._note: ADR-112 / ADR-114 Decision 3. Three new declarative type:dashboard pages plus Engagement, which already existed as an index over engagement-record and had NO menu entry — carding it gives an entry point rather than moving one. ⚠️ THE SCHEMA SLUG IS NOT THE SEED KEY: the seed keys are PascalCase (Decision, VotingRound) and the slugs are kebab-case (decision, voting-round). A widget naming the key renders an empty card and says nothing.

pages.title: Decisions
pages._note: Every filter is scalar equality, the only kind OpenRegister's aggregation endpoint can evaluate. A multi-value or relative-date filter is accepted and then silently not applied — which is how this app's own KPI cards came to show wrong numbers before they were rewritten as custom widgets.

pages.title: Voting
